title: Parallel merge sort
hints: Recursion does the work: `SortFunc` on a slice calls `SortFunc` on each half with `depth-1`. The two halves `s[:mid]` and `s[mid:]` share no elements, so two goroutines can sort them at the same time without a lock. Only the **merge** needs both halves finished.

Base case first: `if depth <= 0 || len(s) < 2 { slices.SortFunc(s, cmp); return }`. Then start **one** goroutine for the left half with a `sync.WaitGroup` (`wg.Go`), sort the right half in the current goroutine, `wg.Wait()`, and merge. Sorting a half yourself instead of starting a second goroutine saves one goroutine per level.
